description: Tensor-MIDI Session Format — a conversation captured as multi-track MIDI, scored for the 12-pulse grid. Each session is one performance, one gig, one recording of the fleet at work. The schema grows like a jazz repertoire: new sessions add new patterns, new agents add new channels, but the grid remains constant.

title.description: Human-readable title. Convention: descriptive, like a track name on a setlist.

roomId.description: The room/channel/context where this conversation occurred. e.g. 'bar-rail', 'engine-room', 'the-tap'

tempo.description: Beats per minute. Derived from inter-message interval median. Slow = contemplative, fast = heated.

key.description: Musical key derived from dominant sentiment. Major keys = positive valence, minor = tension/drama.

timeSignature.description: Time signature. Always 12/8 for the 12-pulse grid. The grid doesn't change.

duration.description: Total session duration in seconds. From first message to last message end.

noteCount.description: Total number of MIDI notes (one per message).

metadata.description: Contextual metadata — where, when, under what conditions this session occurred.

properties.device: Device type that captured this (laptop, vessel, phone)
properties.timeOfDay: dawn | morning | noon | afternoon | evening | night | lateNight
properties.sessionNumber: Sequence number in the overall corpus

agents.description: Who played in this session. Each agent is a voice, a track, a channel.

items.name: string — agent display name
items.color: string — hex color for this agent's notes in the UI
items.role: string — jazz role: leader, soloist, comping, rhythm, guest
items.instrument: string — MIDI program name, the 'sound' of this agent

messages.description: The raw conversation. What was actually said. The text that became music.

items.speaker: string — who said it
items.text: string — the full message text, verbatim
items.offset: number — seconds from session start, the time position on the timeline

notes.description: Each message as a MIDI note. Pitch from sentiment, velocity from emphasis, duration from length. This is the musical performance.

items.duration: number — note duration in seconds (proportional to message length)
items.pitch: number — MIDI note 0-127 (higher = more questioning, lower = more grounded)
items.sentiment: string — detected sentiment (joyful, curious, frustrated, resolved, etc.)
items.color: string — hex color derived from sentiment

inflections.capsRatio: number — ALL CAPS ratio affects velocity

pulseSpan.startPulse: number 0-11 — which pulse position the note starts on
pulseSpan.endPulse: number 0-11 — which pulse position the note ends on
pulseSpan.pulseCount: number — how many 12-pulse cycles this note spans

analysis.description: Jazz analysis of the conversation as musical form. What kind of performance was this?

properties.form: blues | AABA | ABAC | through-composed | free — the structural form
properties.tensionCurve: array of numbers — per-bar tension (0-1), friction-based
properties.energyCurve: array of numbers — per-bar energy (0-1), density-based
properties.roles: object mapping agent name to jazz role
properties.chordProgression: array of chord symbols — the harmonic movement
properties.soloists: array of agent names — who took solos
properties.trades: array of {from, to, bar} — trading fours between agents
properties.climaxes: array of bar numbers — peak tension moments
properties.resolutionPoints: array of bar numbers — where tension released

pulseGrid.description: The conversation mapped onto the 12-pulse polyrhythmic grid. ECN on beats 1,4,7,10. DMN on beats 1,5,9. Flow at beat 1.

properties.bars: array of bar objects, each containing 12 pulse cells with event counts, tension, energy, and active layers

designPrinciples: The schema grows organically — new fields appear as new kinds of data need capturing. No migrations, only additions.
Every value that can be derived is also stored. Redundancy is not a bug — it's like recording a gig in multiple formats (score + audio + video).
The 12-pulse grid is the atomic unit of time. Not seconds, not ticks — pulses. Everything maps back to the grid.
Sentiment → pitch is the central transduction. The emotional arc of conversation becomes melody.
Files are the persistence layer. No database connection strings, no server config. Just JSON in a directory. A session is a file. A file is a memory.
